requiredEdit.why: GitHub Actions run 35276932599 on head fb2adc7e1, job "Unit Tests (4/6)" (ubuntu-latest): six cases of the pin failed with "Expected: 0  Received: 1" at lines 392, 444, 475, 564, 587 and 607 - exactly the six that need the closure to write verdict PASS.
requiredEdit.rootCause: the closure's mainProof verdict requires merge.parentCount === 1, because the loop's merge method is a squash merge. The pin fabricated the merge commit as the AMBIENT checkout's HEAD and had the fake gh report it. On a pull_request event actions/checkout@v6 leaves HEAD at refs/pull/N/merge - for this PR, 6bf5a1c6aa7b58bb2ed443366df5fe3697cbdf1b, whose parents are f018e34cc and fb2adc7e1 - a TWO-parent commit. The closure computed parentCount 2, wrote verdict FAIL and refused with MAIN_PROOF_NOT_PASS, correctly, on the input the pin gave it.
requiredEdit.notAPlatformDefect: the variable is the checkout ref, not the OS. Measured on both: the same fixture exits 0 on Linux with a one-parent merge commit and exits 1 on Windows with a two-parent one.
requiredEdit.decisiveEvidence: gh api repos/:owner/:repo/commits/6bf5a1c6aa7b58bb2ed443366df5fe3697cbdf1b -> two parents; git rev-list --parents -n 1 HEAD in this worktree -> one parent; and an A/B probe on Windows (node v22.22.0) and Linux (WSL Ubuntu-24.04, node v22.23.2, git 2.43.0) in which the parent count is the only variable. Full analysis, per-candidate rulings and commands: evidence/u17b-red-20260917.json -> requiredEditRevision2.
requiredEdit.candidatesRuledOut: (a) a Windows-only fake-gh shape, (b) gh.cmd/PATHEXT resolution, (c) preserveRunLogs refusing on POSIX, (d) a \r\n or path-separator assumption - each ruled out with a measurement, not an argument; see the red receipt.
requiredEdit.fix: scripts/__tests__/roadmap-loop-closure-proof.test.ts only. beforeAll builds a throwaway three-commit git repository under os.tmpdir(); headSha and earlierSha come from it and every closure case runs with --repo-root pointed there, so no case reads the checkout's own HEAD and no checkout ref can change a verdict. expectClosureOk(result) replaces the six bare exit-status assertions with the same condition plus the closure's stderr and stdout in the failure message. Two small dedups came with it: without(args, flag) generalises withoutLedgerDir, and PIN_GIT_ENV + commitAll() replace three copies of the commit-identity block.
requiredEdit.whyNotAProductChange: the one-parent requirement is correct for a squash merge and is pinned by the loop's own merge contract; weakening it to make the pin green would have deleted a real check. Both modules are byte-identical to revision 1.

findingsResolved.resolution: --skip-blob-check is refused whenever the resolved ledger directory is the repository's own (DEFAULT_LEDGER_DIR), compared through realpath and case-folded on win32. The refusal (BLOB_CHECK_REQUIRED) lands immediately after resolveLedgerDir, before the first gh call and before anything is written or copied.
findingsResolved.whyNotAnEnvironmentVariable: ROADMAP_LOOP_PIN=1 is set as easily as the flag is passed. Binding the weakening to a ledger that is not this repository's own means no receipt in this ledger can carry a blob check nobody ran.

findingsResolved.resolution: the Lane A reviewer model is read from the review markdown's `reviewerModel:` header line and trimmed; a review with no such line, or an empty one, is refused (REVIEW_MODEL_MISSING). The value flows into both the review receipt and the unit entry's stageReceipts.review.
findingsResolved.whyTheHeader: 15 of the 18 Lane A reviews already on main carry `reviewerModel:` on its own line beside `reviewedHead:`, which the closure already parses out of the same file, so the value comes from the artefact being receipted rather than from an argument that could contradict it.

findingsResolved.why: the module already records the run before refusing - the FAIL mainProof receipt is written and then the refusal is thrown - and the logs are part of that record. A FAIL is the run whose logs are most wanted, and the worktree is removed after a FAIL just as after a PASS. This resolves the limit the staging README recorded instead of carrying it forward as a non-claim.

nonClaims: Revision 2 was not verified on a Linux CI runner. The fix is verified here by measurement of the mechanism - the parent count of refs/pull/1839/merge, and an A/B probe on Windows and on WSL Ubuntu-24.04 - and by the pin no longer reading the checkout's HEAD at all. The pin itself could not be run on Linux: node_modules is a Windows junction with no Linux @swc native binding, and npm install is forbidden here, so `node node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js` on WSL fails to load its native binding before any test runs. Whether CI is green is a claim only the next CI run can make.
The A/B probe that reproduced the defect is scratch code under the session scratchpad; it was never added to the repository and is not part of the delivery.

The real proof ladder was never run: no build, no Playwright, no jest ladder on a merge commit. Only --dry-run, its dirty refusal taken from this worktree (G9), and a clean dry-run against a throwaway git repository (G10).

roadmap-main-proof.mjs's execution branch - spawning each step, per-step logs, the e2e marker scan, sha256.txt and the post-run dirty count - still has NO test. It is transcribed from the four shell ladders and read, not measured. Testing it needs an injected step runner; that injection point was NOT added, because adding one is a widening of a unit whose brief is to restore the staged modules and resolve two findings.
--runtime-command's shell branch is never executed, only its flag choice.
gh is a fake on PATH in every closure case. That proves the closure's handling of the JSON shape, not the real gh's shape.

The closure generator was never run against the live ledger. Every closure case works on a temporary copy of the ledger directory, and the F3 case works on a throwaway mirror of the three scripts whose own default ledger is a stub - so the guard's sameDir comparison is exercised, but not against this repository's real ledger directory.
G10 proves what the ladder PRINTS, not that any step in it works.
The preserve-before-verdict move is pinned against a fabricated proof directory (nine step logs plus sha256.txt), not against a real proof run.
The 18 cases run on this baseline in this worktree; they were not run on a merge commit.
